## Right-click a bar - **Right-click any bar in the notation** (anywhere on it, or on its grip) for a menu: Copy Bar, Paste Over, Paste After, Duplicate, Insert Empty Bar After, Clear Bar, **Flip Stems in Bar**, a **Bar Voice** submenu (stems up, stems down, auto), **Add Bar to Worksheet**, Play Only Bar / Play All Bars, Move Left, Move Right and Delete Bar. The bar you click becomes the selected bar, and lines that can't work right now are greyed out.
## Worksheets - A new **Worksheet** button sits beside Chart Builder above the notation. It opens the worksheet panel and takes you straight to it. - The worksheet panel has a big blue **New Worksheet** button at the top right, and a "No worksheet yet" message with the same button when you have none. - **Right-click an exercise** on the worksheet for Copy Exercise, Paste Over Exercise, Paste After Exercise, Load onto Grid, Move Up/Down, plus Edit, Rename, Duplicate and Delete. A copied exercise can be pasted into any worksheet. - The worksheet header is tidied so Add Current and Save To are no longer cut off.
## Also in this test build (from 151 to 157) - Worksheet Add Current / Save To use the selected bar, Save offers to update a loaded exercise or Library preset, flip stems, copy/paste/duplicate/insert bars, drag to reorder bars, delete any bar, and the status message no longer covering the top buttons.
This build is 158.

## Worksheets - **Add Current** and **Save To** now use the bar you have selected (the one highlighted in the notation). Before, they used the playhead's bar, which is bar 1 unless something had been played, so a bar you had edited or flipped could be missed. If Play is set to a single bar, that bar is still used. The message tells you which bar was added. - If you load a worksheet exercise onto the grid with a single click, change it and press Save, BeatBake now asks whether to **Update Exercise** too, so the change reaches the worksheet. (Double-clicking an exercise to edit it on the grid already saved straight back and doesn't ask.)
## Also in this test build (from 151 to 156) - Save offers to update the Library preset you loaded, flip stems, copy/paste/duplicate/insert bars, drag to reorder bars, delete any bar, and the status message no longer covering the top buttons.
This build is 157.

## Save now offers to update the Library preset - If you load a groove from your Library, change it (for example flip the stems of a fill) and press Save, BeatBake now asks whether to **Update Preset** too. Before, Save kept your changes in the groove you were working on but left the Library copy as it was, so loading it again gave back the original. - Choose **Update Preset** to keep your changes in the Library, **Keep Library Copy** to leave the preset alone (it won't ask again until you change the groove), or Cancel. - It only asks when the groove really came from that preset: not after you load something else or undo back past the load.
## Also in this test build (from 151 to 154) - Flip Stems (click a notehead, then the button or X), copy/paste/duplicate/insert bars, drag to reorder bars, delete any bar, and the status message no longer covering the top buttons.
This build is 156.

## Fix - The short message that appears when you do something ("Saved", "Bar 4 stems flipped down" and so on) no longer covers the top buttons. It now sits in the empty space at the left of the Play / Tempo row.
## Also in this test build (from 151 to 153) - Flip Stems: click a notehead, then the Flip Stems button or X. - Copy Bar, Paste Over, Paste After, Duplicate Bar and Insert Empty Bar After, with Command-C and Command-V. - Drag a bar's grip to reorder bars, nudge with the arrows, and delete any bar.
This build is 154.

## Flip stems with one click - Click a notehead in the notation (a blue ring shows it is picked), then click **Flip Stems** above the notation or press **X**. The stem flips up or down, and flipping again puts it back exactly as it was. - With no note picked, Flip Stems flips every hand note in the selected bar together. Kick and hi-hat foot stay down. - Click empty space in the notation to un-pick a note.
## Also in this test build (from 151 and 152) - Copy Bar, Paste Over, Paste After, Duplicate Bar and Insert Empty Bar After (right-click a bar's grip, or the "..." Bar actions menu in the Grid toolbar), with Command-C and Command-V. - Drag a bar's grip to reorder bars, nudge with the arrows, and delete any bar, not just the last.
This build is 153.

## Copy, paste, duplicate and insert bars - Right-click a bar's grip (under the notation) for Copy Bar, Paste Over, Paste After, Duplicate Bar and Insert Empty Bar After. The round "..." Bar actions menu in the Grid toolbar has the same actions, plus Delete Bar. - Command-C copies the selected bar and Command-V pastes over it (not while you are typing in a text field). - Paste After, Duplicate and Insert move the later bars along. A groove holds up to four bars.
## Rearranging bars (from 151) - Drag a bar's grip to move it, nudge it with the arrows, or delete any bar (not just the last), so you can keep, say, only bar 4.
This build is 152.

## Rearranging bars - Each bar of the notation has a grip underneath it. Drag it to move the bar: a blue line shows where it will land, and the bar takes its notes, flams, accents, voices and stickings with it. - Arrows on the grip nudge a bar one place left or right (useful when the bar you want is off-screen), and a right-click gives Move Left, Move Right and Delete. - Delete any bar, not just the last: the bin on a bar, or the bin beside Clear Bar. The bars after it slide up, so you can keep only bar 4 of a 4-bar groove. Each move or delete is one Undo step.
This build is 151.

## Worksheets - The worksheet header is tidier: Library, Save/Delete Template and Print are now icons (hover for the name), so Play, Add Current, 1/line and Stickings show in full. - New Export button (two arrows) sends the worksheet to Sibelius, MuseScore, Dorico or Finale, each exercise on its own line.
## Sibelius and MuseScore - Export a groove, song chart or worksheet: File > Export (Command-E), or the Sibelius button above the notation or in Chart Builder. - Import a drum part saved from Sibelius or MuseScore (File > Export > MusicXML there): as a whole new song chart in Chart Builder, or as the first 4 bars of a groove.
## Also since 146 - Bar voice menu for writing fills stems up; rests that respect the beat. - Stickings print on worksheets (Stickings button, on by default).
This build is 150.

## Sibelius and MuseScore - Export a groove, song chart or worksheet to Sibelius, MuseScore, Dorico or Finale: File > Export (Command-E), the Sibelius button above the notation or in Chart Builder, or the arrow on the worksheet Print button. - It opens as an editable drum set part with your stickings, accents, flams, ghost notes, hi-hat "o" and "+", triplets, sections, repeats and 1st/2nd time bars. - Import a drum part saved from Sibelius or MuseScore (File > Export > MusicXML there): as a whole new song chart in Chart Builder, or as the first 4 bars of a groove.
## Also since 146 - Bar voice menu for writing fills stems up; rests that respect the beat. - Stickings print on worksheets (Stickings button, on by default).
This build is 149.

## Writing fills stems up - New "Bar voice" menu next to Clear bar: move every hand note in the bar to stems up (or down, or back to Auto) in one step, triplets included. Kick and hi-hat foot stay below. - Drums in the upper voice keep the note value you entered: an 8th snare no longer turns into a quarter note.
## Rests - Rests never cross a beat: an 8th rest on the & of 1 then a quarter rest on 2. - Half rests start where the gap starts and sit above or below the staff, clear of the notes.
## Also since 146 - Stickings print on worksheets (Stickings button, on by default).
This build is 148.

## Print stickings on worksheets - New Stickings button next to 1/line-2/line on the worksheet. When it's on (the default), your R/L stickings print on the worksheet. - Turn it off for a cleaner page. Worksheets without stickings print the same either way.
This build is 147.

## Printing - Worksheets print on exactly the pages they need, with no blank page at the end. - Exercises are centred on the page, with matching left and right margins. - The dot of a dotted rest sits next to the rest in printed worksheets.
## Notation - Put a Pedal Hi-Hat (foot) note where an open hi-hat closes: the foot shows below the stave and a "+" above it. The Close tool moves the "+" to the note you mark. - Sticking letters sit clear of hi-hat "o" and "+" marks and accents, on screen and in print.
## Worksheets (since 137) - Double-click an exercise to edit it on the grid; changes save into the exercise. - Drag exercise cards to reorder them. - Rename with the pencil or right-click. Replacing an exercise keeps its name. - Card icons are visible in dark mode and when selected.
This build is 146.

## Notation - Put a Pedal Hi-Hat (foot) note where an open hi-hat closes: the foot shows below the stave and a "+" above it. The Close tool moves the "+" to the note you mark. - Sticking letters sit clear of hi-hat "o" and "+" marks and accents, on screen and in print. - In printed worksheets, the dot of a dotted rest now sits next to the rest instead of the following note.
## Worksheets (since 137) - Double-click an exercise to edit it on the grid; changes save into the exercise. - Drag exercise cards to reorder them. - Rename with the pencil or right-click. Replacing an exercise keeps its name. - Card icons are visible in dark mode and when selected.
This build is 145.

## Open hi-hats close where you want - Put a Pedal Hi-Hat (foot) note where the hi-hat closes. The foot shows below the stave and a "+" shows above it at the same beat. - The next hand hi-hat no longer gets a stray "+". The Close tool moves the "+" to the note you mark. - Sticking letters now sit clear of hi-hat "o" and "+" marks and accents, on screen and in print.
## Worksheets (since 137) - Double-click an exercise to edit it on the grid; changes save into the exercise. - Drag exercise cards to reorder them. - Rename with the pencil or right-click. Replacing an exercise keeps its name. - Card icons are visible in dark mode and when selected.
This build is 144.

## Open hi-hats close where you want - Put a Pedal Hi-Hat (foot) note where the hi-hat closes. The foot shows below the stave and a "+" shows above it at the same beat. - The next hand hi-hat no longer gets a stray "+". - The Close tool moves the "+" to the note you mark, instead of adding a second one.
## Worksheets (since 137) - Double-click an exercise to edit it on the grid; changes save into the exercise. - Drag exercise cards to reorder them. - Rename with the pencil or right-click. Replacing an exercise keeps its name. - Card icons are visible in dark mode and when selected.
This build is 143.

## Open hi-hats close where you want - Put a Pedal Hi-Hat (foot) note where the hi-hat closes. The notation shows the foot and no longer adds a "+" to the next hand hi-hat. - The Close tool now moves the "+" to the note you mark, instead of adding a second one.
## Worksheets (since 137) - Double-click an exercise to edit it on the grid; changes save into the exercise. - Drag exercise cards to reorder them. - Rename with the pencil or right-click. Replacing an exercise keeps its name. - Card icons are visible in dark mode and when selected.
This build is 142.

## Edit worksheet exercises on the grid - Double-click an exercise card to open it on the grid. Every change you make is saved into that exercise automatically. - A banner above the grid shows which exercise you're editing. Click Done when you've finished. - Rename an exercise with the pencil beside its name, or right-click > Rename Exercise.
## Also since 137 - Drag exercise cards to reorder them. - Card icons are visible in dark mode and when selected. - Replacing an exercise keeps its name.
This build is 141.

## Worksheets - Drag an exercise card to move it. A blue line shows where it will land: drop on the left half of a card to go before it, the right half to go after it. Escape cancels. - The move, duplicate and delete icons on exercise cards are now visible in dark mode and when the card is selected. - Rename an exercise on the worksheet page: double-click its name, or right-click and choose Rename Exercise. - Replacing an exercise keeps its name and only updates the notation.
This build is 140.

## Worksheet exercise names - Rename an exercise right on the worksheet page: double-click its name, or right-click and choose Rename Exercise. - Replacing an exercise now keeps its name and only updates the notation. Previously the name was overwritten with the Groove name, so renames didn't stick.
Also includes everything in 137. This build is 138.

## Faster chart tempo - Song Chart Builder now has a tempo slider, like the main window. - Click and drag the BPM number: right or up to speed up, left or down to slow down. Hold Option for fine control. - The arrows still step 1 BPM at a time, and a whole drag undoes in one step.
Also includes everything in 136. This build is 137.

## Safer saving - If your library can't be read in full, BeatBake now keeps a copy of the original file, opens everything it can, and tells you. Nothing is overwritten. - Pending saves finish when you close Chart Builder or quit. If a save fails on quit, you can cancel and keep working. - New or Open over an edited chart asks you to Save, Discard, or Cancel. - Groove undo now goes back 100 steps (was 5).
## Song Chart Builder - Choose individual bars or grouped rests when adding bars and sections. - Delete Bar button beside Add Bar. - Left/Right arrows move between bars, Up returns to bar 1, and the selected bar scrolls into view. - Chart Builder uses a single window: opening it again brings your chart forward. - Faster drawing and playback on long charts.
## Playback and licensing - Steadier timing at fast tempos. - The seven-day offline grace starts as soon as you activate your licence.
This build is 136 (was 133).
